title: Rebalance gRPC After Scaling Out
description: A gRPC service sits behind an L4 network load balancer. During a traffic spike the team scales from 4 to 8 instances, but the new instances stay nearly idle while the original four remain overloaded. Clients hold a few long-lived HTTP/2 connections each. What is the best fix?

options.text: Change the L4 policy from round robin to least connections.
options.explanation: The balancer still places connections, not requests. Existing long-lived connections stay where they are, so the new instances still see little load.

options.text: Enable sticky sessions so each client consistently reaches one backend.
options.explanation: Stickiness pins load even more firmly to the original backends and does nothing to spread requests.

options.text: Balance per request with an HTTP/2-aware L7 proxy or client-side load balancing, and set a maximum connection age so clients reconnect.
options.explanation: gRPC multiplexes many requests on one connection, so balancing must happen per request. A maximum connection age makes old connections cycle onto new instances.

options.text: Probe health more frequently so the new instances are marked ready sooner.
options.explanation: The new instances are already healthy; they simply receive no new connections. Faster probes do not move existing traffic.
